name: Chi-Square DCT Coefficient Analysis
description: Applies the Chi-Square goodness-of-fit statistical test to Block Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) coefficient distributions. In natural photographs, the statistical distribution of AC coefficients follows highly predictable, smoothly decaying Laplacian patterns. Generative AI models, which do not organically compress light through a physical lens and quantization matrix, often synthesize or embed frequency anomalies that deviate wildly from standard camera quantization tables.
algorithm: Statistical Goodness-of-Fit on DCT AC Coefficients
mechanism: The algorithm calculates the histogram of DCT AC coefficients across 8x8 pixel blocks and applies the Chi-Square test to compare the observed distribution against the theoretical expected natural logarithmic decay (Laplacian distribution). When an image is natively generated by a camera and then saved as a JPEG, the coefficients fall neatly into predefined quantization bins. However, AI, which generates pixels directly in latent space and applies algorithmic smoothing, frequently creates 'impossible' coefficient distributions—such as skipped bins, unnatural clustering, or abnormal steganographic-like perturbations that fail the Chi-Square null hypothesis.
parameters: Block Size: 8x8 DCT, Test Type: Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit, Target Coefficients: AC Components, Significance Level: p < 0.05
accuracy: Moderate (72-83%) - Excellent at identifying algorithmic anomalies or steganographic payloads, but highly dependent on the image being a JPEG and can be tricked by secondary re-compression.
source: Westfeld & Pfitzmann (2000) / Fridrich et al. (2003) - Attacks on Steganographic Systems
useCase: Detecting AI-generated anomalies manifesting as unnatural compression footprints, spotting hidden steganographic data, and verifying if a JPEG's structure aligns with a natural photographic origin.

references.title: Westfeld, A. & Pfitzmann, A. (2000). Attacks on Steganographic Systems. Information Hiding.
Fridrich, J. et al. (2003). Detection of Double-Compression in JPEG Images. Information Hiding.

strengths:
• Relies on a rigorous, mathematically proven statistical framework (Chi-Square).
• Calculates extremely fast over quantized coefficients, without needing to fully decompress the image into the spatial domain.
• Provides a stark, quantifiable p-value representing mathematical confidence of anomaly presence.
• Highly effective at spotting structural deviations caused by AI upscalers or hidden algorithmic watermarks.
limitations:
• Only effective on images that utilize block-DCT mapping (JPEGs). Completely powerless on lossless formats (PNG, RAW) or non-DCT spaces.
• Highly sensitive to extreme compression; heavy social media re-encoding can smooth out both natural and artificial anomalies indiscriminately.
• Can flag aggressive but authentic manual Photoshop editing simply because the software re-aligns the DCT grid.
